candidates.name: cfpb-complaints-database
candidates.what_it_holds: LA Times Data Desk's committed copy of the full CFPB Consumer Complaints Database as downloaded 25 April 2018 - a frozen point-in-time snapshot (not a live API pull) of what was at the time ~1M+ consumer financial complaints across all products/companies nationwide.
candidates.why_useful: This is exactly the kind of point-in-time vintage the brief wants (gap #4): a dated, immutable complaint-database snapshot from 2018 that can be diffed against a fresh 2026 CFPB pull to see how Airbnb-BNPL-adjacent (Affirm/Klarna) complaint volume and travel/lodging-merchant complaint mentions have grown, without any lookback bias.
candidates.time_coverage: snapshot as of 2018-04-25 (covers complaints filed up to that date, likely back to ~2011-2012 database inception)
candidates.size_hint: full national complaint DB (hundreds of MB typically at that vintage)

candidates.name: cfpb_data_downloader
candidates.what_it_holds: Small Python tool that calls the CFPB's public Consumer Complaints Database Trends API and downloads complaint-trend data (by product, company, issue, date range) to local files - a one-command pull, no auth needed.
candidates.why_useful: Turns the live CFPB complaint database into a repeatable, scriptable pull we can run at each guide date going forward, so we can build our own point-in-time vintage register of BNPL/travel-refund complaint counts (mentions of Airbnb, Affirm, Klarna, Afterpay) rather than relying on someone else's stale snapshot.
candidates.time_coverage: whatever the live CFPB API currently serves (2011-present)

candidates.name: cfpb.api
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (also forked/maintained at riddlet/cfpb.api) that wraps the CFPB public Consumer Complaint Database API for programmatic querying/filtering by product, company, state, date.
candidates.why_useful: Alternative-language client for the same official complaint database; useful if the team's pipeline is R-based, and as a cross-check implementation against the Python downloader above.

candidates.name: CFPB_Complaint_Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis notebook plus derived extracts working over the full CFPB Consumer Complaint Database described as 11M+ records, with NLP performed on consumer complaint narratives and breakdowns by company/product/response time.
candidates.why_useful: Full-size recent pull of the national complaint corpus with narrative text already parsed; a 'Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service' / prepaid-card / BNPL-lender filter over the narratives could surface Airbnb-refund-via-Affirm/Klarna complaint language for a qualitative RNPL-friction read.
candidates.time_coverage: recent pull (repo active late 2025), full CFPB history to date

candidates.name: mcp-cfpb
candidates.what_it_holds: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server wrapping the free, no-auth CFPB Consumer Financial Protection Bureau complaint database API, exposing search/query tools an LLM agent can call directly.
candidates.why_useful: Would let an agent query live CFPB complaint counts/trends (e.g. 'Money transfer' or 'Credit card/Prepaid card' complaints mentioning specific BNPL lenders) on demand without hand-rolling API calls; very fresh (13 Sep 2026), so still active.

candidates.name: BNPL_Merchant_Dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Research pipeline scraping the official BNPL provider merchant directories (Affirm, Klarna, Afterpay, Zip, Sezzle) for merchant name/category/provider/URL, matched via SEC ticker files + SEC CompanyFacts API to public parent companies, building a quarterly firm-panel 2015-2026. Current checkpoint: 8,470 unique merchants, 144 public-company merchant rows / 127 unique parents, 4,675 firm-fiscal-quarter SEC records (93.6% revenue coverage), adoption-date verification via Internet Archive CDX (no fabricated dates, unresolved dates left UNKNOWN).
candidates.why_useful: Directly on-theme: a maintained, methodologically careful cross-reference of which public companies (and whether Airbnb-adjacent travel merchants) accept which BNPL provider, plus the SEC-filing financial panel around adoption timing - this is the closest thing found to 'is Airbnb/travel-lodging a BNPL merchant and when did BNPL options appear' with a reusable, non-fabricated methodology. Also a template for checking Airbnb's own presence in Affirm/Klarna merchant directories.
candidates.geography: US (SEC-filer universe), BNPL provider directories are broader
candidates.time_coverage: merchant directories current; SEC financial panel 2015-2026

candidates.name: Global-Debt
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed IMF Global Debt Database extract: unbalanced panel of 190 advanced/emerging/low-income economies, annual government/corporate/household/external debt as % of GDP, 1950-2022 (columns: country, debt-category/inflation indicator, annual percentages).
candidates.why_useful: Household-debt-to-GDP by country is a cross-country consumer-leverage/credit-stress proxy that could feed the regional consumer-strength split (NA/EMEA/LatAm/APAC) the model already tracks; longer history (to 1950) than anything currently held on consumer credit.

candidates.name: Customer-Segmentation-USA-EDA-
candidates.what_it_holds: EDA repo built on the Federal Reserve's Survey of Consumer Finances (SCF) microdata - household income, debt, and asset holdings by demographic group; the SCF itself is the Fed's public source, this repo is a worked example pointing to/using it.
candidates.why_useful: SCF is a genuine primary source for US household debt/asset composition by income tercile - useful as a slower-moving benchmark for consumer leverage capacity around travel spend, though this specific repo is a low-value student EDA wrapper rather than a data mirror.

candidates.name: better-business-bureau-bbb-complaint-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: A scraper targeting Better Business Bureau (BBB) complaint pages to extract complaint text/metadata for a given company.
candidates.why_useful: Method only (no committed data) that could, if run against Airbnb's or a BNPL provider's BBB profile, produce a complaint-volume/complaint-text time series; per the rules this is catalogued as a method and left unrun (BBB scraping is a terms-of-service call for a human).

candidates.name: bulk-bbb
candidates.what_it_holds: Bulk BBB reviews/complaints extractor tool (scraper), generic across companies.
candidates.why_useful: Same class as above: a reusable BBB scraping method that could be pointed at Airbnb or Affirm/Klarna if a human clears the terms-of-service question; not run here.

candidates.name: ae-cfpb-complaint-benchmarking
candidates.what_it_holds: dbt/Snowflake project benchmarking consumer complaints across 10 major US banks using the full CFPB database (cited at 16.9M rows) sourced via BigQuery's public `bigquery-public-data.cfpb_complaints` dataset; pipeline code is committed, the 16.9M-row table itself lives on BigQuery (Google-hosted mirror of the CFPB DB, updated regularly).
candidates.why_useful: Confirms and documents the existing free, queryable BigQuery mirror of the full national CFPB complaint database (`bigquery-public-data.cfpb_complaints`) with a ready-made dbt transformation layer as a template; that BigQuery table is itself the more directly useful object (queryable with a free-tier GCP account, no scraping) for extracting BNPL-lender or travel/lodging-refund complaint slices.
candidates.time_coverage: CFPB DB inception (~2011) to present, refreshed periodically
candidates.license: unspecified pipeline code; underlying data is public-domain US government

candidates.name: CFPB-Complaints
candidates.what_it_holds: SQL query file (no raw data committed) that reconstructs an 18-field, 2M+-row CFPB complaint dataset from Google's public BigQuery mirror (`bigquery-public-data.cfpb_complaints`), plus a mortgage-focused PDF report as an example of use.
candidates.why_useful: Second independent confirmation of the free BigQuery CFPB mirror and a ready SQL query to pull it; low incremental value beyond the ae-cfpb-complaint-benchmarking entry above but corroborates the access path.
candidates.time_coverage: CFPB DB inception to pull date

notes: Hard blocker this run: the shared WebSearch tool budget (200/session) was already exhausted by other scouts before I made my first call, so all four planned WebSearch queries failed immediately. Worked around it with (a) WebFetch against github.com/search HTML pages (worked twice, then 429/rate-limited for the rest of the hour), (b) WebFetch against Bing/DuckDuckGo (DuckDuckGo returned a bot CAPTCHA every time; Bing rendered only its own generic/branded results, never actual site:github.com hits, so it was not useful for this modality), and (c) the unauthenticated public GitHub REST search API via curl (https://api.github.com/search/repositories) — NOT the `gh` CLI, so it draws from a separate, lower-traffic quota; this became the main channel and worked well until it too hit the unauthenticated rate limit once (recovered after ~60s). Recommend other web-modality scouts try the same api.github.com/search/repositories curl fallback if WebSearch is dry for them too. Substantively: real BNPL usage-statistics data (Klarna/Affirm public disclosures, CFPB's own Sep-2022 BNPL market-monitoring aggregated-lender data extracted to CSV) was not found anywhere on GitHub in the time available — what exists is almost entirely (a) generic/synthetic BNPL 'credit risk' Kaggle-style student EDA projects with fabricated or LendingClub-substitute data (excluded per instructions), and (b) CFPB complaint-database re-analyses, none of which isolate an Airbnb- or travel-specific complaint slice pre-built. The most useful finds were the BigQuery mirror confirmation (bigquery-public-data.cfpb_complaints, free, queryable, no scraping) and the 2018 point-in-time complaint-database snapshot (datadesk/cfpb-complaints-database) for vintage comparison. Fed G.19 consumer credit and NY Fed household-debt-and-credit-panel searches on the GitHub API turned up nothing beyond generic fraud-detection/Kaggle projects — no GitHub mirror of either series was found; FRED already covers G.19-adjacent series per CONTEXT.md so this may be a genuine gap rather than a search failure. Worth a follow-up scout: query the BigQuery public dataset directly (not GitHub) for CFPB complaints naming 'Airbnb', 'Affirm', 'Klarna', or 'Afterpay' in the narrative field, and check whether CFPB's original BNPL market-monitoring report PDFs (Sep 2022, aggregated data from Affirm/Afterpay/Klarna/PayPal/Zip) have ever been transcribed to CSV anywhere on GitHub or Zenodo.
